summary: The MCP stdio host lists and reads supported resources, and now always completes the MCP handshake even when a project's descriptors fail to load, verified against a real spawned process.
worksToday: Serves supported resources over an MCP duplex transport, and over a real stdio child process against the actual repository root.
Preserves text and binary resource payload distinctions.
Completes MCP initialize and serves a structured elegy://host/diagnostics resource when descriptor composition fails, instead of exiting before the handshake.
Exposes --preflight to check a project's descriptor configuration without opening the MCP transport, wired into .elegy/checks.json and CI.
limitations: Does not make every Elegy surface a working MCP tool: list_tools is always empty and call_tool always errors by design.
No clean packaged installation driven by a real external MCP client (e.g. an actual Claude Desktop session) has been reviewed; only a real spawned-process test in source.
supportedEnvironments: Windows source build; portable Rust implementation
installation: Build from source with cargo build -p elegy-host-mcp, or `just install-mcp` for a receipted local install.
invocation: Run elegy-run --project <path to a project with descriptors>. Use --preflight to check the project without opening the MCP transport.

evidence.summary: The workspace package compiled as part of the source suite.
Real spawned-process MCP handshake tests against the actual repo root and a degraded-mode project passed; see docs/adr/2026-09-05-mcp-host-descriptor-contract.md.
